correctness.rationale: Independently, for any vertex pair the inserted edge and the intercepted path form the unique cycle. If the two vertices project to positions at distance a on the original span ℓ, the two cycle arcs give a decrease a²/(ℓ+1/w); the series tails cancel. Summing yields the stated gain: centering the clipped ramp at ℓ/2 gives sum −(p−q)ℓ/2 and sum of squares ℓ(3nℓ−2ℓ²+2)/12. The resulting imbalance penalty eliminates nonmaximal placements at fixed span. At odd tail sum the two even-tail neighbors have total numerator strictly larger than twice the odd numerator, by (n−ℓ)²/2, and average denominator equal to the odd denominator; thus one strictly wins. The only missing neighbor case is span two at even n, where span three wins both at w→0 in the numerator and at w→∞ after dividing by span, hence at every w>0. Subtracting adjacent centered scores gives the stated crossing and its sign, with positive crossings exactly at k<K. To check ordering directly, write the crossing in x as 3(1/x+1/(x−2))(n+1−x)/(4x−3n−4); both positive factors increase as successive spans x decrease in the admitted range. After the final crossing range each next shorter span is strictly dominated by its longer neighbor for every finite w. These adjacent comparisons yield exactly the claimed winners and two-way ties for all n, including K=0. An independent cycle-arc enumeration verifies all nonedges for orders 4–32 at 125 exact rational probes, covering every equality and every open phase in that range.
residual_risks: The finite replay corroborates the proof; the conclusion for unbounded n and the full continuum of finite positive w uses the adjacent-score argument. Infinite conductance is not covered.
